first.title: How long until the first record is ready
first.explain: From when the posting was found, and from when its application was begun, to the first record ready to send. Counted for the applications whose first record was made in this period. A long wait from finding often means postings wait in the queue or are not started automatically.

backlog.title: What waits for you
backlog.explain: How long the cards on the to-do page waited from appearing to being dealt with, for those dealt with in this period; and the oldest of the ones still open.
backlog.sub: {handled} dealt with in this period · {open} open now

reason.not_started: never started (queued, or not started automatically)
reason.waited_for_you: stopped at a step that waited for you
reason.under_way: still under way when it closed

asked.title: Questions asked again and again
asked.explain: Questions the agent had to ask you, or answers you corrected, in more than one application. Each is one your profile could answer by itself: write it into the profile and the agent answers it from then on.
asked.sub: Counted once per application, for the applications begun in this period.
asked.question: Question
asked.done: Written into your profile; the agent answers it by itself from now on

unknown.title: Submissions whose outcome was not known
unknown.explain: Submit was pressed but the page that says it went out was not seen. Such an application is settled by the employer's confirmation mail, or by you saying whether it went out. This is how long that took, and which are not settled yet.
unknown.settled: {n} settled: {out} went out, {mail} known from a mail

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.sub: Everything with a time: deadlines, interviews, assessments, offers to answer, people to get back to, and your own notes.
calendar.started: The agent is starting the application

form.title: What
form.timeHint: Leave empty for the whole day.

alarm.title: Reminders
alarm.hint: Reminders go to your Telegram or Discord and appear at the top of the to-do page. When the date moves, they move with it.
alarm.hintAllDay: This item is for a whole day: its reminders come in the morning (the hour is in the settings).

share.title: The calendar in your calendar app
share.exportText: What the page shows now (this view, these filters) as a calendar file, with each item's reminders. Open it with your calendar app to import it.
share.subscribeText: Give this address to your calendar app ("add calendar from URL"): it reads it again by itself and stays up to date. It contains titles, times, links and a line about each item - never your answers or the text of mails.
share.copyFailed: Could not copy: select the address and copy it
share.localOnly: This address works only on this computer: a calendar app here can subscribe, one on your phone cannot. To subscribe on the phone, make the program reachable from it first (Settings → Remote access).
share.reachable: This address works wherever the program can be reached from - the same as the links in notifications.
share.renewAsk: The old address stops working. A calendar app subscribed to it has to be given the new one. Make a new address?
share.renewed: New address made; the old one no longer works

reminders.title: Calendar reminders
reminders.intro: What each kind of item gets by itself when it appears - in minutes before it (1440 = one day, 60 = one hour), several separated by commas. Each item's own reminders are changed in its panel on the calendar.
reminders.morning: Whole-day items in the morning at
reminders.quiet: A reminder in the quiet hours waits for them to end
reminders.hint: Without the box ticked, a reminder goes out at its time even in the quiet hours: you set the time yourself.

purpose.label: What it is:
purpose.mine: a file of yours, for any application
purpose.made: put together from your files for one application

files.wentNowhere: not used in any application yet

filter.inUse: Only what an application in progress uses

files.clean: Archive {n} old file | Archive {n} old files
files.cleanAsk: Archive {n} file made for applications that are over (or a version no longer used)? They are kept - archived files can be shown again - and nothing being prepared uses them. | Archive {n} files made for applications that are over (or versions no longer used)? They are kept - archived files can be shown again - and nothing being prepared uses them.
files.deleteAsk: Delete the {n} selected file for good? It cannot be undone. A file that went out with an application is archived instead: it is what was sent. | Delete the {n} selected files for good? It cannot be undone. Files that went out with an application are archived instead: they are what was sent.
files.deletedKept: {n} deleted; {kept} that went out with an application archived instead
